\[
\begin{pmatrix} a \\ -1 \\ c \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -11 \\ -16 \\ 25 \end{pmatrix},
\]

we start by using the formula for the cross product of two vectors \(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \\ u_3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2 \\ v_3 \end{pmatrix}\):

\[
\mathbf{u} \times \mathbf{v} = \begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\
u_1 & u_2 & u_3 \\
v_1 & v_2 & v_3
\end{vmatrix}.
\]

Applying this to our vectors \(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ -1 \\ c \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}\), we get:

\[
\begin{pmatrix} a \\ -1 \\ c \end{pmatrix} \times \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}
\mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\
a & -1 & c \\
7 & 3 & 5
\end{vmatrix}.
\]

Expanding this determinant, we have:

\[
\begin{vmatrix}
a & -1 & c \\
7 & 3 & 5 \\
\end{vmatrix} = a \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 7 & 5 \end{vmatrix} - (-1) \begin{vmatrix} 7 & 5 \\ 7 & 5 \end{vmatrix} + c \begin{vmatrix} 7 & 3 \\ 7 & 3 \end{vmatrix}.
\]

Calculating each of the 2x2 determinants, we get:

\[
\begin{vmatrix} 3 & 5 \\ 7 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = (3 \cdot 5) - (5 \cdot 7) = 15 - 35 = -20,
\]

\[

\]

\[
\begin{vmatrix} 7 & 3 \\ 7 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = (7 \cdot 3) - (3 \cdot 7) = 21 - 21 = 0.
\]

Substituting these values back into the expansion, we get:

\[
a(-20) + 1(0) + c(0) = -20a.
\]

\[
